observed_2012_source.citation: Perry LE, Pannell JR & Dorken ME (2012) PLoS ONE 7:e35597
observed_2012_source.original_oh_definition: Relative seed production of hermaphrodites versus females: o_h = sigma_h/sigma_f
observed_2012_source.comparable_ratio: Female seed production relative to hermaphrodite equals 1/o_h within each experimental plot, as a descriptive reciprocal
observed_2012_source.female_seed_advantage_condition: o_h strictly less than 1 (female relative seed production higher)
observed_2012_source.source_precision: All Table 2 o_h and offspring sex morph proportions are printed with two decimals; each is rounded, +/- 0.005 for uncertainty bounds
observed_2012_source.parental_female_fraction: Low density 16/49, high density 75/225; female included in every experimental treatment cell

observed_same_plot_counts.proof_ceiling: No causal mediation or allelic CMS frequency observed

observed_2012_source.interpretation: Printed relative reproductive success via seed output can favor female morphology even while next-generation female phenotype declines under the same plot's mating/segregation structure

model_2025_prior_art.citation: Nguyen MT & Pannell JR (2025), The evolution and maintenance of trioecy with cytoplasmic male sterility, Heredity 134:1–9
model_2025_prior_art.study_type: Published theoretical recursion and simulations, not field experiments
phenotypes: XY CMS-carrying male with partial nuclear Y restoration

model_parameter_definitions.g: Female seeds relative to hermaphrodite seeds
model_parameter_definitions.alpha: Male pollen relative to hermaphrodite pollen
model_parameter_definitions.e_m: Proportion of male pollen aborted by CMS, zero means fully restored

source_results: Males can hinder rare cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) invasion but enable stable trioecy in model parameter regimes
With some hermaphrodite selfing and a Y-linked partial fertility restorer, negative frequency dependence can maintain three sex morphs even with no pollen limitation
Males siring females' sons create offspring that cannot maternally transmit the CMS cytoplasm, limiting the spread of CMS
When CMS fully eliminates male pollen (e_m=1), the maintenance regime differs and male restoration is not available
Order of invasion can alter which sexual system forms or whether extinction is approached in some model scenarios
The model is based on nuclear and cytoplasmic genetic transmission, not an architecture-independent universal SLK theorem
model_2025_prior_art.source_prior_art_boundary: This paper explicitly distinguishes invasion and equilibrium maintenance with partner/sex composition; SLK cannot claim first discovery of this phenomenon

cross_taxon_direct_selection_prior_art.citation: Laugier F et al. (2025), Cytoplasmic Male Sterility Declines in the Presence of Resistant Nuclear Backgrounds. The American Naturalist 206:16–30
cross_taxon_direct_selection_prior_art.study_type: 11-generation experimental evolution in freshwater hermaphroditic snail, not plant trioecy
cross_taxon_direct_selection_prior_art.treatment: CMS-bearing mitochondrial haplotypes experimentally placed in nuclear background rich in male fertility restorers
cross_taxon_direct_selection_prior_art.result: CMS mitochondrial haplotypes declined across 11 experimental generations; study authors estimated approximately 20% relative fitness disadvantage in that nuclear genetic context
cross_taxon_direct_selection_prior_art.independent_result: Separate isolated-snail hatching assay found reduced hatch success of CMS carriers, but did not account for all ~20% fitness disadvantage
cross_taxon_direct_selection_prior_art.interpretation: Direct evolutionary loss of a CMS cytotype under a compatible nuclear-restorer context can occur in an animal; cannot substitute for CMS allele lineage tracking in Mercurialis
limitations: Different mitochondrial species, animals rather than flowering plants
Restorer-rich genetic background not a direct SLK phenotype module
Reported ~20% value is author estimate; no primary raw records refitted in SLK
11 experimental generations not a macroevolutionary origin of sex morphs

claim_limits: 2012 female relative seed production is reproductive output proxy and not mother-genotype transmission fitness; 19 plot-level signs do not represent 19 independent evolutionary origins
2012 source Table2 reports offspring phenotypes after seed germination, not cytoplasmic haplotype frequencies or paternal parentage
Female reproductive morphology and CMS genotype should not be assumed identical in all plots without direct genotyping
2012 study plot genetic backgrounds and density treatments differ; observed seed advantage and decline simultaneously is not controlled manipulation of CMS fitness
2025 Heredity model provides prior theoretical mechanism but is NOT fitted to observed 2012 20 plot-specific relative seed ratios
2025 invasion and maintenance regimes depend on genetics, pollen limitation and selfing assumptions; never import one paper's illustrative parameter values as observed Mercurialis field estimates
2025 Physa snail direct evolutionary experiment addresses restoration-mediated cytonuclear selection, not floral multifunctionality or three-sex coexistence in plants
Do not add 2012, 2025 Heredity and 2025 snail as multiple independent plant experimental invasion replications
All new SLK plot-level arithmetic uses previously published 2012 plot summaries; no original raw genotypes, lineage data, or 2024 Figshare accession were retrieved
SLK Phi, g0 and Delta_R are NOT estimated or demonstrated in nature by this synthesis
